# Welcome {background-color="#16181A" style="color:#F7F6F3"}

## What you are walking into

This course asks one question in ten different ways:

> **When can a number about the past be used to make a claim about the future?**

- The methods are standard: least squares, penalisation, trees, factors, causal ML.
- The data are European, international, and messy on purpose.
- The discipline is knowing **what your estimate does not entitle you to say.**

::: {.muted}
Ten sessions of method. One question throughout.
:::

## Three distinctions we will not let go of

::: {.tight}
1. **A scenario is not a forecast.**
   *Europe 2031* is a conditional narrative — a stress test, not a prediction.
   You will read it as a set of assumptions you can measure.

2. **Prediction is not inference.**
   "How well does this predict?" and "what is the effect of X?" are different
   questions, answered by different estimators, with different guarantees.

3. **A construct is not a measurement.**
   An "AI exposure index" is something we built. Session 09 is about being
   honest about that.
:::

## What this session's pre-work is

Four things, before you arrive:

| # | Task | Time |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | **Build your workstation** — these slides | 60–90 min |
| 1 | Read *Europe 2031* | 30 min |
| 2 | Review three concepts | 15 min |
| 3 | Run the verification script | 5 min |

::: {.warn}
**Session 1 does not include installation time.** Arriving without a working
environment means you cannot take part in the lab.
:::

# The stack {background-color="#16181A" style="color:#F7F6F3"}

## What we install, and why

| Tool | What it is | Why this one |
|---|---|---|
| **VS Codium** | VS Code with telemetry removed | Your work touches confidential and licensed data. The editor should not phone home. |
| **Python 3.10+** | The analysis language | Everything in the course runs here. |
| **Ollama** | Runs LLMs on *your* machine | No API key, no per-token cost, no data leaving your laptop. |
| **Qwen 2.5 Coder** | The model Ollama serves | Small enough for a laptop, strong at code. |
| **aider** | An AI agent in your terminal | Reads and edits your files, and commits. |

## The principle behind the stack

Every piece runs **locally**.

::: {.check}
**The test that matters.** When your environment is finished, turn off your
wifi and ask the model a question. If it still answers, your setup is
genuinely local — and your data never left the room.
:::

::: {.muted}
This is not ideology. In Session 09 you work with licensed text, and in the
group project you may work with data you are not permitted to upload anywhere.
:::

## Where do I type this? {#where}

**Read this slide before you type anything.** It is the single most common
source of lost time.

Two kinds of instruction appear in these slides, and they are always labelled:

::: {.get}
download
:::
Go to a website in your browser and run an installer. No typing.

::: {.where}
VS Codium terminal
:::
Type it in the terminal **inside VS Codium** — never the macOS Terminal app,
never PowerShell on its own.

## Why always the VS Codium terminal

::: {.tight}
- It opens **in your project folder**, so `git` and `python` act on the right files
- It sees the `.venv` you activate; a separate Terminal window does not
- It is the same on macOS, Windows and Linux, so these slides work for everyone
:::

::: {.check}
**Open it now:** ``View → Terminal``, or ``Ctrl+` `` (the backtick key, above
Tab). A panel appears at the bottom. That panel is where every command below
goes.
:::

::: {.warn}
If a command fails, check *where you typed it* before you check anything else.
:::

## Before you start

You need:

- A laptop with **8 GB RAM minimum** (16 GB is much more comfortable)
- **Administrator rights** to install software
- About **10 GB free disk space** — the model files are large
- 60–90 minutes, uninterrupted

::: {.warn}
Do this on the machine you will actually bring to class. A working setup on a
desktop at home is of no use in the lab.
:::

# Step 1 — VS Codium {background-color="#16181A" style="color:#F7F6F3"}

## Install VS Codium

::: {.get}
download
:::

Go to **vscodium.com** and download the build for your operating system.

::: {.muted}
This is the one step that cannot use the VS Codium terminal — you are installing
the thing that provides it.
:::

::: {.cols}
::: {}
**macOS**

Download the `.dmg`, open it, drag **VSCodium** to Applications.

If macOS refuses to open it: right-click the app → **Open** → **Open**.
:::
::: {}
**Windows**

Download the *User Installer* `.exe` and run it.

Tick **"Add to PATH"** when the installer offers it.
:::
:::

**Linux:** use your package manager, or the `.deb` / `.rpm` from the same page.

::: {.check}
**Check.** VS Codium opens and shows the Welcome tab.
:::

## Meet the two panels you will live in

::: {.shot}
[ VS Codium window ]

Left: **Explorer** (your files) · Bottom: **Terminal** · Right: **Continue** (chat)
:::

Two things to find right now:

- **The Explorer** — `View → Explorer`, or `Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+E`
- **The integrated Terminal** — ``View → Terminal``, or ``Ctrl+` `` (backtick)

::: {.warn}
The **Terminal** is where most of this course happens. If you have never used a
command line, that is fine — every command you need is on these slides.
:::

## Step 2 — Extensions

Open the Extensions panel: `Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+X`. Install three:

| Extension | Search for | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| **Python** | `ms-python.python` | Syntax, linting, environment selection |
| **Jupyter** | `ms-toolsai.jupyter` | Run notebooks inside the editor |
| **Continue** | `Continue.continue` | The chat sidebar, wired to your local model |

::: {.warn}
VS Codium uses the Open VSX registry, not Microsoft's Marketplace. Most
extensions are there. If one is missing, the course does not depend on it.
:::

# Step 3 — Python {background-color="#16181A" style="color:#F7F6F3"}

## Install Python

::: {.get}
download
:::

Go to **python.org/downloads** and install **Python 3.11 or 3.12**.

::: {.warn}
**Windows: tick "Add python.exe to PATH"** on the first installer screen. It is
easy to miss, and without it nothing below works.
:::

::: {.muted}
macOS ships an old Python that is not suitable. Install a current one anyway.
:::

## Check Python is there

::: {.where}
VS Codium terminal
:::

```bash
python3 --version
```

::: {.check}
Prints `Python 3.11.x` or `3.12.x`.

On Windows, if `python3` is not found, try `python --version`.
:::

::: {.warn}
If it says *command not found*, the PATH box was not ticked. Re-run the
installer — do not try to work around it.
:::

## Create the environment

::: {.where}
VS Codium terminal
:::

First `File → Open Folder…` and choose your course folder. Then:

```bash
python3 -m venv .venv
```

This makes a private package folder for this course, so it cannot break your
other work.

## Activate it

::: {.where}
VS Codium terminal
:::

```bash
# macOS / Linux
source .venv/bin/activate

# Windows (PowerShell)
.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1
```

::: {.check}
Your prompt now starts with `(.venv)`. **Every command from here on assumes you
see that.**
:::

## Install the packages

::: {.where}
VS Codium terminal · with `(.venv)` showing
:::

```bash
pip install -r requirements.txt
```

numpy, pandas, scikit-learn, statsmodels, matplotlib and the rest. A few minutes.

::: {.check}
```bash
python -c "import numpy, pandas, sklearn; print('ok')"
```

prints `ok`.
:::

# Step 4 — Ollama and Qwen {background-color="#16181A" style="color:#F7F6F3"}

## Install Ollama

::: {.get}
download
:::

Go to **ollama.com/download**, choose your operating system, and run the
installer. This works on macOS, Windows and Linux.

::: {.muted}
You may see a one-line `curl … | sh` command on the web. Ignore it — the
installer does the same thing and there is nothing to mistype.
:::

::: {.warn}
On macOS, **open the app once** after installing. It puts the `ollama` command
in place and starts the background service.
:::

## Check Ollama is there

::: {.where}
VS Codium terminal
:::

```bash
ollama --version
```

::: {.check}
Prints a version number.
:::

::: {.warn}
*Command not found?* Close the terminal panel and open a new one — a new
terminal picks up the changed PATH. On Windows, restart VS Codium.
:::

## Pull Qwen 2.5 Coder

::: {.where}
VS Codium terminal
:::

Choose by the RAM in your machine. Rough rule: **model size + 2 GB free**.

| Your machine | Model | Command |
|---|---|---|
| 8 GB RAM | `qwen2.5-coder:3b` | `ollama pull qwen2.5-coder:3b` |
| 16 GB RAM | `qwen2.5-coder:7b` | `ollama pull qwen2.5-coder:7b` |
| 32 GB+ / Apple Silicon | `qwen2.5-coder:14b` | `ollama pull qwen2.5-coder:14b` |

You also need the embedding model for Session 10:

```bash
ollama pull nomic-embed-text
```

::: {.warn}
This downloads several gigabytes. Do it on a good connection, **not** ten
minutes before class.
:::

## Verify the model

::: {.where}
VS Codium terminal
:::

```bash
ollama list
```

You should see your model listed. Now talk to it:

```bash
ollama run qwen2.5-coder:7b "Explain the bias-variance tradeoff in three sentences."
```

Type `/bye` to leave the chat.

::: {.check}
**The real check.** Turn off your wifi and run that command again. It should
still answer. That is what "local" means.
:::

# Step 5 — The CLI agent {background-color="#16181A" style="color:#F7F6F3"}

## Talking to Qwen the way I talk to Claude

The Continue sidebar is useful for questions about a selected block of code.

But the way this course actually works — and the way I work in front of you —
is an **agent in the terminal**: something that reads your files, edits them,
and commits, while you steer it in prose.

That tool is **aider**, and it runs against your local Qwen.

::: {.muted}
Same shape as the workflow you have seen me use. Different engine, and it is
running on your laptop.
:::

## Install aider

::: {.where}
VS Codium terminal · with `(.venv)` showing
:::

```bash
python -m pip install aider-install
aider-install
```

## Point aider at Ollama

::: {.where}
VS Codium terminal
:::

```bash
# macOS / Linux
export OLLAMA_API_BASE=http://127.0.0.1:11434

# Windows (PowerShell) — then open a new terminal
setx OLLAMA_API_BASE http://127.0.0.1:11434
```

## Give Ollama a real context window

::: {.warn}
**This step is not optional.** Ollama defaults to a **2k** context window and
then *silently discards* whatever does not fit. Your agent will appear to
"forget" the file you just gave it.
:::

Start the server with a larger window:

::: {.where}
VS Codium terminal 1
:::

```bash
OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH=8192 ollama serve
```

Leave that terminal running. Open a **second** terminal for aider.

::: {.muted}
In VS Codium: the `+` icon in the terminal panel splits off a new shell.
:::

## Run the agent

::: {.where}
VS Codium terminal 2
:::

```bash
cd /path/to/your/repo
aider --model ollama_chat/qwen2.5-coder:7b
```

::: {.warn}
Note the prefix: **`ollama_chat/`**, not `ollama/`. The second one exists and
behaves worse.
:::

## Ask it for something

You are now at a prompt. Ask in plain language:

```
> add a function that loads data/spine/core.parquet
  and prints the number of rows per country
```

aider writes the code, shows you a **diff**, and asks to apply it.

::: {.check}
Read the diff before you accept. That habit is the whole skill.
:::

# The worked example {background-color="#16181A" style="color:#F7F6F3"}

## Two terminals

**Terminal 1** — the model server, left running:

::: {.where}
VS Codium terminal 1
:::

```bash
OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH=8192 ollama serve
```

**Terminal 2** — inside your course folder:

::: {.where}
VS Codium terminal 2
:::

```bash
source .venv/bin/activate
aider --model ollama_chat/qwen2.5-coder:7b
```

## Ask for something real

::: {.where}
At the aider prompt
:::

```
> create explore.py that loads data/spine/core.parquet,
  prints the shape, and shows mean gdp_pc_eur by year
```

aider proposes a diff. You read it. You accept it.

```bash
python explore.py
```

## What just happened

::: {.check}
You ran a model **on your own hardware**, had it write code against real data,
reviewed the change, and accepted it — **without sending one byte to anyone's
API.**
:::

::: {.muted}
Every lab this term is a variation on those two terminals.
:::

## Why we do it this way

::: {.tight}
- **The data stay put.** Some of what you use this term cannot legally be uploaded.
- **The cost is zero.** No key, no quota, no bill at the end of the month.
- **The record is honest.** The diff shows exactly what changed, and why.
- **The skill transfers.** This is how the work is actually done now.
:::

::: {.warn}
The model is a **junior collaborator with no accountability.** It will produce
confident, wrong code. Every line you accept is a line you are claiming as
correct. Read the diff.
:::

# If it breaks {background-color="#16181A" style="color:#F7F6F3"}

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Fix |
|---|---|
| `ollama: command not found` | Reopen the terminal; on Windows, restart VS Codium |
| Model answers very slowly | Use a smaller model (`:3b`); close other applications |
| aider "forgets" your file | You skipped `OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH=8192 ollama serve` |
| `connection refused` from aider | The `ollama serve` terminal is not running |
| `pip` fails on install | Check `(.venv)` is in your prompt |
| `python3` not found on Windows | Try `python`; if still missing, PATH was not ticked |

::: {.muted}
Still stuck? Ask Qwen — that is itself a test of whether your setup works.
:::
